exposure: Type of neuraxial anesthesia (spinal, epidural, or combined spinal-epidural)
outcome: Intraoperative change in mean arterial pressure
cohort: 108 parturient women with obesity and pregnancy-induced hypertension undergoing cesarean section
finding: While combined spinal-epidural anesthesia took longer to administer, it was associated with shorter surgery time, more stable blood pressure during surgery, lower rates of nausea and vomiting, lower rates of low blood pressure during surgery, and better Apgar scores compared to spinal or epidural anesthesia alone.
